structured_output.strongest_bear_case: This token is a copycat that borrowed another project's links, not that project's token. Its packet points to buyxhandles.com (a third-party X-username marketplace) and the BuyXHandles X account. But that website's footer names a different contract as the project's token: JCvGrCbiHc84qCEDowgeuue7iXNoGgpCQstgoGYhFUCK. Our token (7dPoC1oc...) is one of at least 11 HANDLES-named tokens launched within about 45 minutes of each other, several of them before it, including the site's own. The story itself is not new: X announced its handle marketplace in October 2025, and the site says it is not affiliated with X Corp. The trading looks bot-driven. Unique buyers were 2,088 but unique sellers only 87. In the last 5 minutes, 57 wallets made 354 buys. Hourly volume was about 40 times liquidity. GMGN flags 51 bundler wallets. The creator has launched 9 tokens and GMGN marks the creator's position as closed. The logo appears on 5 other tokens. There is no DexScreener profile. Most likely this is a short-lived clone in a crowded launch rush that will fade as attention moves to the website's token or disappears.
